The evidence chunks are essentially identical across all genes (all rated critic_relevance=2/5, none directly mentioning the specific gene). Since the literature evidence doesn't differentiate between genes, I must rely on prior biological knowledge. The phenotype profile (lymphoid hyperplasia, decreased anti-polysaccharide antibody response, recurrent otitis media, bronchiectasis, recurrent sinopulmonary infections, splenomegaly, anti-Ro/SS-A positivity) is consistent with a primary antibody deficiency/CVID-like syndrome. Among the candidates, TRAF3 has known roles in B-cell survival and NF-κB signaling relevant to antibody production; CCDC22 (X-linked) is associated with immunodeficiency with recurrent infections; GON7 is part of the KEOPS complex linked to IEI. None are classic CVID genes, but TRAF3 has the strongest immunological rationale.
